obstetricBands.title: Swedish obstetric NEWS2 chart by Hein, Lindroos and Åmark, reproduced in the 2025 SFOG course
obstetricBands.scope: Resolve the four overlapping endpoints in the 2025 WEST ONEWS2 table. WEST defines pathway eligibility and colour thresholds.

extraction_notes: Clinical categories and care needs/processes come from pages 10–48. NEWS2, ONEWS2, GCS, mNIHSS, monitoring, orders, and SBAR are supporting materials and are not separate clinical categories.

The category pages are the source for criteria. The overviews on pages 3–5 sometimes differ from the category pages. Differences are retained unless a resolution is recorded. Trauma alert colors come from page 3.
Line breaks and extra spaces have been normalized. Clinical conditions and thresholds in the findings have not been converted into automated decision rules.
An empty criteria list means that the category has no color-coded criteria of its own or that its criteria appear in subcategories.

notes: A patient with medication poisoning that can cause organ damage should be assessed in a medical emergency department.
Page 37 clarifies the warning signs. The explanations are retained separately.

clarifications.text: Suicide attempt. Assess the level of observation required and assess using NEWS2.

Self-harm with a strong wish to die now, or a threat of a suicide attempt in progress. Inform the nurse in charge immediately. Assess the level of observation required. Do not leave the patient alone. Are means of suicide available?
Self-harm. The patient intentionally injures themselves in the emergency department.

Ongoing violence. The patient attacks people or objects, for example by kicking, hitting, throwing or knocking things down, or smashing windows. Contact a physician immediately. Consider compulsory measures.

Physically threatening behavior. Clear intent to threaten another person physically, for example through an aggressive stance, grabbing their clothes, or raising a hand threateningly. Contact a physician. Offer sedative medication and assess the level of observation required.

Verbally threatening behavior. An outburst that goes beyond raising the voice and is intended to humiliate or frighten another person. Offer sedative medication and assess the level of observation required.

Delirium tremens is a serious medical condition requiring treatment. Contact a physician immediately if suspected. Onset is usually 2–4 days after stopping alcohol. Signs include picking at objects, delusions, marked agitation, confusion, and visual or auditory hallucinations. Assess using NEWS2. Elevated pulse, blood pressure, and temperature are common.

Marked withdrawal symptoms with physical signs and risk of seizures and delirium tremens. Contact a physician. Use a single room, offer sedative medication, and assess the level of observation required.

New behavioral disturbance. Hallucinations and delusions may be new or reflect worsening psychosis. Confusion develops over hours to days. Mania may present with marked overactivity, pressured speech, and disinhibition. Other signs include marked anxiety, emotional lability, inhibition, or dissociation.

categories.category: Frailty in older adults – care needs

criteria.text: Frail older adult by FRESH screening
criteria.definition: Age ≥75 years plus a modified FRESH score ≥2 defines frailty. Living in residential care scores 2 points. Reduced endurance, general tiredness or reduced energy for <2 months, frequent falls or fear of falling, and needing help with shopping each score 1 point. Assign at least yellow priority and see the patient first within their color group.

conflicts.finding: Four ONEWS2 cells overlap at RR 10, systolic BP 80, diastolic BP 90 and pulse 60.
conflicts.handling: Apply the contemporaneous Swedish obstetric NEWS2 chart at the four overlapping endpoints. RR 10 scores 0, systolic BP 80 scores 2, diastolic BP 90 scores 1 and pulse 60 scores 0.

conflicts.finding: Category uses potassium ≥6.0 with ECG changes. Overview uses >6.0.
conflicts.handling: Use the inclusive category threshold. Potassium exactly 6.0 with ECG changes qualifies for the red finding.

conflicts.finding: Overview includes acute dizziness at 4.5–24 hours or unknown onset and mNIHSS ≥2 in red. The category and extract name suspected stroke in that row.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied Östra neurology category rows and their onset and mNIHSS qualifiers. An overview-only dizziness combination does not create a selectable finding.

conflicts.finding: Östra supplies six gynaecology subcategories, including time-limited green criteria. SkaS has a different category structure. In the non-pregnant bleeding subgroup the supplied JSON gives heavy vaginal bleeding yellow; the SkaS female genital category gives it orange. The supplied bleeding category also gives it orange.
conflicts.handling: Assign the identical heavy vaginal bleeding criterion orange in both adult pickers. The pregnancy-specific heavy bleeding criterion remains red. Preserve the original yellow on the non-pregnant source row. Apply 07:00 inclusive to 16:00 exclusive at local measurement time to timed green rows.

conflicts.finding: SkaS lists ongoing vomiting before week 18 as yellow here. Östra includes a separate early-pregnancy nausea and vomiting pathway.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied early-pregnancy nausea and vomiting pathway with its own criteria. The SkaS overview adds no separate finding.

conflicts.finding: Overview qualifies hanging/strangulation by visible or audible injury; the category lists it without that qualifier.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied red hanging or strangulation criterion. Visible or audible injury is not an additional selection condition.

conflicts.finding: The extract describes withdrawal with risk of both seizure and delirium tremens, while the SkaS category says either.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied Östra orange criterion for somatically affected withdrawal with risk of both seizure and delirium tremens.

conflicts.finding: The SkaS overview includes gurgling with foaming breathing; the category describes foaming breathing.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied red dyspnoea with foaming breathing criterion. Gurgling is not an additional selection condition.

conflicts.finding: The compact SkaS table omits saturation ≥93% on air from Scale 2. The RCP chart explicitly assigns 0.
conflicts.handling: Score saturation of 93% or above on room air as zero on prescribed Scale 2. Use the separate supplemental-oxygen branch when oxygen is administered.

conflicts.finding: SkaS prohibits clinical down-prioritisation from red or orange.
conflicts.handling: A clinician may select any of the four colours. That single effective colour takes precedence. Store the calculated result and provenance separately.

conflicts.finding: Overview describes ingestion of a battery or magnet. The category and extract specify a button battery or at least two magnets.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied orange criterion for a button battery or at least two magnets.

conflicts.finding: The overview includes symptomatic smoke inhalation (orange), finger or toe dislocation (yellow), and newly impaired or worsened outwardly aggressive behaviour with inability to care for oneself (yellow). These are not standalone criteria in the extract under those labels.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied category inventory. Symptomatic smoke inhalation, finger or toe dislocation and the overview-only behavioural description are not additional standalone options.

conflicts.finding: SkaS specifies more than 1,000 V or lightning. The extract refers to high voltage or lightning without the number.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied red high-voltage or lightning criterion. The clinician selects this finding.

conflicts.finding: The supplied joint criterion says interarticular; the SkaS category describes intra-articular swelling.
conflicts.handling: Use the supplied Östra joint criterion and wording. A clinician selecting it records yellow.
